target_customer: US health systems and provider groups that pay coders and fight claim denials
problem: Medical chart coding is manual, slow and error prone, driving denials and lost revenue. Arintra uses AI to code charts autonomously and writes codes back into the EHR.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS for health systems, revenue assurance platform
product_category: Healthcare AI, autonomous medical coding and revenue cycle

founders.name: Nitesh Shroff
education: PhD in Machine Learning, University of Maryland
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: early engineer at Zoox, founding engineer at Light, 30+ patents and publications.

founders.name: Preeti Bhargava
education: PhD in Computer Science, University of Maryland, College Park
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: data scientist roles, 30+ US patents.

competitors.name: Fathom
competitors.what: Autonomous medical coding platform using deep learning
competitors.funding_then: $46M Series B announced November 2022, after the batch; an aggregator lists an earlier Series A in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading full charts, applying specialty coding rules and writing back to EHRs required ML plus deep EHR integration, hard for a small team in 2022.

defensibility.rationale: EHR integrations, KLAS and HITRUST credentials and customer coding data build stickiness, but rivals such as Fathom and CodaMetrix pursue the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors raised large rounds (CodaMetrix $55M Series A in February 2023). No acquirer action against Arintra found.

market_need_then: Coder shortages and claim denials strained provider revenue cycles. Autonomous coding vendors attracted investment from 2021 onward.

brand_strength.rationale: Invented name with no brand story found. Credibility comes from KLAS spotlight and funding coverage rather than brand pull.

outcome_analysis: Arintra raised a $21M Series A in August 2025 led by Peak XV and a $25M Series B in August 2026 led by Define Ventures, with health system customers named on its site. Its path fits an enterprise AI play with real integrations and credentials. The seed amount is not public, and several funded rivals compete for the same wedge.
notes: Seed amount not found; Peak XV reportedly backed the founders earlier through its Surge program. Total raised of $51M per Series B coverage versus CB Insights $21.5M reflects its lag. Headquarters reported as San Francisco, Austin or Bay Area in different places. Competitor list has only one entry dated after the batch; CodaMetrix (founded 2019 per a profile, Series A February 2023) and Nym Health are later or undated. Series A dated August 12 or 26, 2025 by different outlets, so month only is used. Series B announced August 26, 2026.
